claims.text: The MgAlCuZnGd alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
Rapid cooling after induction melting produces a non-equilibrium MgAlCuZnGd microstructure containing finely dispersed metastable intermetallic phases.
Annealing MgAlCuZnGd at approximately 450 °C for several hours coarsens its intermetallic phases toward an equilibrium state.
The fine intermetallic phases in as-cast MgAlCuZnGd are enriched in Mg and Gd.
Fine Mg- and Gd-enriched intermetallic phases act as preferential sites for early oxide nucleation.
High-temperature exposure selectively oxidizes Mg and Gd in the as-cast alloy.
Selective Mg and Gd oxidation produces a scale predominantly containing MgO and Gd oxides.
The MgO- and Gd-oxide-rich scale is coherent, dense, and protective.
Intermetallic phase size, morphology, and spatial distribution influence corrosion performance.
Stable intermetallic phases and passive surface oxides can impede corrosion-front propagation.
Coarse intermetallic phases in equilibrium-annealed MgAlCuZnGd produce less uniform and more porous oxide scales than fine intermetallic phases.
The oxide-scale chemistry and continuity control high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The as-cast alloy will exhibit lower corrosion current density in room-temperature 3.5% NaCl than the equilibrium-annealed alloy.
The as-cast alloy will form a more uniform, adherent, and protective scale at 600, 750, and 900 °C than the equilibrium-annealed alloy.
TEM-EDS and depth-profiled XPS can determine the morphology, chemistry, and elemental distribution of Mg- and Gd-containing oxide scales.
Failure of the as-cast samples to show a statistically significant corrosion-current reduction or a uniform MgO- and Gd-oxide-enriched scale would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism attributes improved chloride corrosion resistance to an oxide scale formed during high-temperature exposure, but the specified room-temperature NaCl test does not state that corrosion specimens are first subjected to high-temperature oxidation. Thus, the experiment as written does not directly test the proposed oxide-scale-to-corrosion pathway.
